title: TCJA 2017 state and local tax deduction cap

legislative_document.title: Public Law 115-97: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act

provisions.label: Cap on state and local tax deduction
provisions.summary: Limits the itemized deduction for state and local taxes to 10000 dollars for most filers during the federal individual tax changes enacted by Public Law 115-97.

claims.claim: The provision is narrow enough to track as a discrete analysis unit because it changes the treatment of one itemized deduction category.
Expected effects vary across taxpayers because use of the deduction depends on itemization and exposure to state and local taxes.

narrow_benefit_indicators.label: Geographic concentration
narrow_benefit_indicators.rationale: The affected deduction is connected to state and local tax exposure, so benefits and burdens may be geographically uneven.

narrow_benefit_indicators.label: Household-specific exclusion
narrow_benefit_indicators.rationale: The POC does not evaluate household records and therefore cannot classify individual household effects.

model_scenarios.label: Canonical current-law base qualitative screen
assumptions: Only public statutory text and public aggregate analyses are used.
No household financial records are collected, transmitted, or stored.
The scenario identifies questions for later modeling rather than estimating household tax liability.
outputs: Flag provision for aggregate distributional review.
Record uncertainty around geography, itemization, and interaction with other TCJA provisions.
limitations: This scenario identifies qualitative questions only.
It does not estimate taxpayer liability or distributional magnitudes.

expected_outputs.plain_language_summary: Public Law 115-97 capped the federal itemized deduction for state and local taxes. This POC records the provision, evidence, uncertainty, and qualitative distribution questions without household-level tax modeling.
known_limits: No broad bill ingestion is performed.
No full tax microsimulation is performed.
No live congressional monitoring is performed.
No household financial data is transmitted or stored.
